Article Title: 'Spreading propaganda against Ayodhya out of fear': Yogi Adityanath targets SP, Congress

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday accused the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress of spreading "propaganda" against Ayodhya, claiming that the two opposition parties were "uncomfortable" with the development of the temple town and the infrastructure projects being undertaken across the state."People are now maligning Ayodhya out of fear. They are spreading propaganda against Ayodhya because they know that if this journey of heritage and development continues in the same manner, the politics of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress will be buried forever," PTI quoted the chief minister as sayiing. He was addressing a Diwali programme in Gorakhpur."Those who once created an identity crisis for the state will now face a crisis of their own political identity. If this journey continues with the same strength and unity, the Congress and the Samajwadi Party will themselves face an identity crisis," he added.Adityanath's remarks came a day after he took an apparent swipe at Samajwadi Party president and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.According to SP leader Pawan Pandey, Akhilesh Yadav and his family will visit the temple on December 12 to offer prayers.This would be the SP chief's first visit to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024."Those who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathi-charge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising. Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints. Let them repent for their actions," Adityanath said in Ayodhya on Saturday without naming his predecessor."There was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga," he added.In 1990, Uttar Pradesh Police opened fire on "kar sevaks" (volunteers) marching towards the Babri Mosque, which stood at the erstwhile disputed site in Ayodhya. Akhilesh Yadav's father Mulayam Singh Yadav was Uttar Pradesh chief minister at the time.The mosque was demolished on December 6, 1992.In November 2019, a Constitution bench of the Supreme Court ruled in favour of the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath accuses Samajwadi Party and Congress of spreading "propaganda" against Ayodhya. He says the opposition parties are "uncomfortable" with the development of the temple town. His remarks come a day after he took an apparent swipe at Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed visit to the Ram Temple.

Article Title: 'Karnataka needs no permission for Mekedatu': DK Shivakumar on Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's letter to PM Modi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Sunday asserted that there is "no need of permission" to build the Mekedatu reservoir across the Cauvery river, which has been at the centre of a long-standing water-sharing dispute between Karnataka and neighbouring Tamil Nadu.Shivakumar's remarks came after his Tamil Nadu counteprart C Joseph Vijay wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In his letter, Vijay urged PM Modi to ensure that Karnataka is not granted any clearance to construct the Mekedatu dam without the consent of the other Cauvery basin states, including Tamil Nadu."I hope that Tamil Nadu's chief minister know the law of the land. No need of permission from anyone. The Supreme Court has already given permission that Karnataka is eligible to build the dam on its own site. And it has put a condition that we should give them 177 TMC of water. That is the condition," ANI quoted the Karnataka chief minister as saying.Shivakumar claimed that the Mekedatu reservoir would ultimately benefit Tamil Nadu more than Karnataka."Tamil Nadu will have more benefit from the Mekedatu reservoir. Balance it is called a balancing reservoir," he said.He further said that Karnataka had identified 5,400 hectares of forest land for compensatory afforestation to meet environmental requirements.The process is underway, after which the state will approach the water commission for clearance.Shivakumar reassured Vijay that Karnataka would honour its commitments and not misuse the water stored in the reservoir."I appeal to the Tamil Nadu chief minister; please send a team. We will not misuse this. We stand by our word," he stated.He furher called for cooperation between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, saying the two states should respect the Supreme Court's verdict and work together on water-sharing issues."There's no question of fighting. The fighting days are over. The Supreme Court has given a verdict. Let us respect the law of this land. Let us work together. Let us share water," he added.He also highlighted the Cauvery's importance for drinking water, agriculture, livestock and industries in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Kerala.Describing the Cauvery basin as a gift to the country, Shivakumar urged Vijay to strengthen ties between the states and work towards farmers' welfare.
Article Summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar says there is "no need of permission" to build the Mekedatu reservoir across the Cauvery river. Tamil Nadu counteprart C Joseph Vijay wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Vijay urged PM Modi to ensure that Karnataka is not granted any clearance to construct the dam.

Article Title: INDIA bloc stages mock arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Bengaluru protest: Watch
Article Text:
INDIA bloc stages dramatic mock arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR row

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday held a state-level protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged manipulation of electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Video footage from the rally showed party workers enacting the arrest of Gyanesh Kumar as part of the demonstration.The protest, which began at 11 am and was scheduled to continue until 2 pm, was organised by the Congress, CPI(M), CPI, CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc and Samajwadi Party, along with other progressive parties, social organisations and student and youth groups involved in the anti-SIR agitation.The demonstration was presided over by Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President BK Hariprasad.Multilingual film actor Prakash Raj, CPI(M) state secretary Prakash K, CPI state secretary Sathi Sundaresh, CPI(ML) Liberation state secretary Clifton D'Rozario, Forward Bloc president JR Shivashankar and Samajwadi Party president N Manjappa also participated in the protest.Representatives of various organisations, including Sarvodaya Karnataka, Eddelu Karnataka, the Federation of Dalit Organisations and the Republican Party of India, attended the rally. Police personnel were deployed in adequate numbers at Freedom Park to maintain security and manage the gathering.The protest was held as part of the INDIA bloc's wider agitation against the SIR exercise and its demand for the CEC's resignation. It follows a demonstration organised by the opposition alliance at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1.On Wednesday, Hariprasad said the Bengaluru rally was a continuation of the November 1 protest and that leaders of several INDIA bloc parties had agreed to participate."In continuation of the protest we had on November 1, the entire INDIA bloc alliance is organising a massive protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru. All our CPI(M), Forward Bloc, Samajwadi Party... and Muslim League leaders have agreed to participate in this," Hariprasad said.He also said the agitation would be extended to districts across Karnataka, with party units asked to organise simultaneous demonstrations at the block level."This protest will continue in Karnataka in almost all districts at the block level. Tomorrow, we have requested all our district units to simultaneously hold protests against SIR and Gyanesh Kumar and demand his resignation," he said.
Article Summary: The protest was held as part of the INDIA bloc's wider agitation against the SIR exercise and its demand for the CEC's resignation. The demonstration was presided over by Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee President BK Hariprasad.

Article Title: 'From India to Pakistan, everyone invited': Anant Singh on daughter's grand wedding
Article Text:
Singh said everyone who had shown affection towards his family was welcome, regardless of where they came from

NEW DELHI: Expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh said invitations for his daughter's grand wedding are being sent to people across India and Pakistan, insisting that political differences have no place at family celebrations. He said he would invite leaders across party lines, including Former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar and RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav.Speaking about the wedding preparations, Singh said everyone who had shown affection towards his family was welcome, regardless of where they came from."Everyone who has shown us love will come. The public is like God to us; whoever comes from wherever will be a gift to me. We are sending invitation cards to everyone. I want all my friends, well-wishers and people associated with us to attend. Everyone is invited. We are contacting everyone whose phone numbers we have. Not just Bihar, invitations are being sent across India and Pakistan. Are the invitations meant only for people in Bihar? They are for everyone, everywhere. We will invite everyone. There is no ruling party or Opposition at a wedding. Such divisions exist during elections and when seeking votes, but not at weddings and family celebrations.Yes, we will invite everyone, including Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav," he said.The wedding comes amid a turbulent political phase for Singh, who was expelled from the JD(U) along with his wife, former MLA Neelam Devi, for six years over alleged anti-party activities in October.The party's Bihar unit president Umesh Singh Kushwaha had announced the decision, accusing Singh of defying party directives, using insulting language against its top leadership and campaigning for a rival candidate in the recent legislative council elections.Despite being a JD(U) MLA, Singh had openly campaigned for Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh against the party's nominee, MLC Neeraj Kumar, in the Patna Graduates' constituency election. The JD(U) also wrote to the Bihar Assembly Speaker seeking the termination of Singh's membership under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution. Neelam Devi's primary membership was also terminated over her alleged involvement in anti-party activities.The expulsion was followed by another setback for Singh in the Dularchand Yadav murder case. On October 30, he said he would comply with the Supreme Court's direction to surrender by December 1. The court issued the directive while hearing a plea seeking cancellation of the bail granted to him by the Patna High Court in March.Singh, who was arrested earlier in the case for allegedly orchestrating Yadav's murder in October last year, maintained that he had faith in the judiciary and expected to secure bail again after subsequent hearings.
Article Summary: Expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh says political differences have no place at family celebrations. He said he would invite leaders across party lines, including Former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar and RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav. Singh said everyone who had shown affection towards his family was welcome, regardless of where they came from.

Article Title: 'Will never visit Ram Temple': TMC's Kirti Azad invokes Sita's Agni Pariksha in attack on BJP

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress MP Kirti Azad on Sunday hit out at the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) over its repeated references to the Ram Temple, accusing the party of using religious sentiments for political gains. He said he had visited the Kamakhya Temple but had never visited the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and had no intention of doing so in the future.His remarks come amid a political row over Samajwadi Party (SP) supremo and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Akhilesh Yadav 's proposed visit to the Ram Mandir and Hanumangarhi temple in Ayodhya on December 12.The proposed visit has drawn criticism from the BJP, which has termed it a political exercise ahead of the elections and accused Yadav of seeking electoral mileage through visits to prominent religious sites.Speaking to news agency IANS, Azad questioned why the BJP repeatedly invoked the Ram Temple and accused the party of misusing temple donations."I do not understand why this Bharatiya Janata Party, which is involved in extortion and stealing donations, keeps talking about the Ram Temple. I have not visited the Ram Temple; I have visited the Kamakhya Temple. Are they suggesting that a person is not a Hindu if they worship Goddess Kamakhya? I worship Goddess Kamakhya, but I have not visited the Ram Temple," he said.Referring to Goddess Sita's birthplace and the episode of her Agni Pariksha, Azad questioned the circumstances surrounding her subsequent abandonment."I belong to the birthplace of Mata Sita. Mata Sita had to undergo the Agni Pariksha, and even after passing it, she was abandoned. Is it right for any human being to treat his wife this way -- to make her undergo the Agni Pariksha and then abandon her even after she passes it? This is not right. I visit Kamakhya Temple and Tripura Sundari Temple. Does that mean I am not a Hindu?" theTMC MP said.Reiterating his stand, Azad told IANS, "I have not gone to Ram Temple, nor will I ever go. I'll go to Mathura."He further accused the BJP of exploiting religious sentiments for political purposes and said the party had failed to establish the ideals of Ram Rajya in the country."They are doing this for politics and are orchestrating robberies and thefts at every temple. They do not have any other issue than Ram. The BJP has not brought Ram Rajya but Ravan Rajya in the country," he added.
Article Summary: Trinamool Congress MP Kirti Azad hits out at the Bharatiya Janata Party over its repeated references to the Ram Temple. He accuses the party of using religious sentiments for political gains. His remarks come amid a political row over Samajwadi Party (SP) supremo Akhilesh Yadav's proposed visit to Ram Mandir and Hanumangarhi temple in Ayodhya.

Article Title: Not a relative: HC quashes dowry case against woman accused only of affair with complainant’s husband
Article Text:
File photo : Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court File photo - High court.(With Akhef's story) Aurangabad,TOI,Photo by Snehil Sakhare

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court has quashed a criminal case against a Bengaluru-based woman who was arraigned in a matrimonial dispute solely on the allegation that she was in an illicit relationship with the complainant’s husband.Justice Sushil M Ghodeswar, in an order passed last week, allowed the woman’s plea under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, challenging an FIR registered at Chakur police station in Latur district on June 4, 2020. The FIR had invoked sections 498-A (cruelty by husband or relatives), 323 (voluntarily causing hurt), 504 (intentional insult) and 506 (criminal intimidation), read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (IPC).According to the complainant, who got married on May 27, 2013, she was harassed by her husband and in-laws over a demand of Rs 50 lakh to buy a flat in Bengaluru. She alleged that her husband introduced the Bengaluru woman as his friend despite being in an illicit relationship with her, assaulted her in a drunken state on March 11, 2020, and that her in-laws forced her to undergo an abortion in 2017.After a chargesheet was filed, the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC), Chakur, took cognisance of the case on Dec 21, 2024, and issued summons to all accused, including the Bengaluru woman.Appearing for the applicant (Bengaluru woman), advocate Ganesh Gadhe argued that she was neither related to the husband nor his family and was residing in Bengaluru. He contended that the allegations against her were vague, unsupported by any specific overt act, and that none of the witness statements implicated her in any offence.Assistant public prosecutor M A Aher, and advocate H B Nandagawale represented the complainant and argued that the chargesheet contained sufficient material and that the Bengaluru woman’s role should be tested during trial.HC relied on Supreme Court’s rulings in State of Haryana vs Bhajan Lal (1992), U Suvetha vs State (2009), and Dechamma I M @ Dechamma Koushik vs State of Karnataka (Dec 4, 2024). The apex court had held that a woman with whom a husband allegedly had an extra-marital relationship was not a ‘relative’ of the husband under Section 498-A.After examining the FIR and witness statements, Justice Ghodeswar observed that the complaint was “lodged as a result of matrimonial differences” between the complainant and her husband. “The only allegation against the applicant is that she was in an illicit relationship with the husband. The applicant is neither related to the husband by blood nor by marriage, and therefore, she cannot be said to be a ‘relative’ of the husband so as to attract Section 498-A,” the court said.The judge further noted that the allegations regarding dowry demand, assault and forced abortion were directed against the husband and in-laws, and that “no specific incident, date or overt act” had been attributed to the applicant to attract offences under sections 323, 504 and 506 IPC. “Even if the allegations are taken at their face value, no offence is made out against the applicant,” the high court held.Invoking the need “to prevent abuse of the process of law and to secure the ends of justice,” the court quashed the FIR, the cognisance order and all consequential proceedings against the Bengaluru woman, while allowing the case to continue against the remaining accused.
Article Summary: Bengaluru-based woman was arraigned in a matrimonial dispute solely on the allegation that she was in an illicit relationship with the complainant's husband. Justice Sushil M Ghodeswar, in an order passed last week, allowed the woman’s plea under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Police inspector, allegedly drunk, assaults complainant on Sahakarnagar police station premises
Article Text:
Assistant commissioner of police Gajanan Pawar is conducting an inquiry against the inspector

Pune:

TOI





An inspector of Sahakarnagar police station assaulted a complainant on the station premises allegedly in an inebriated state on Friday night over a trivial issue.Senior inspector Vitthal Pawar of Sahakarnagar police station said, “We have registered a case against the inspector on Friday night and investigating the matter further.” He has also been booked under the Maharashtra Prohibition Act, but police did not confirm if he was taken to a hospital for a medical test.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone II) Milind Mohite told, “The inspector was scheduled to go on leave for five days from Saturday. It is not known why he went to the police station in an inebriated condition. We have ordered an internal inquiry into the matter. Assistant commissioner of police Gajanan Pawar is conducting an inquiry against the inspector.”Senior police inspector Pawar said, “A passenger travelling on a PMPML bus came to the police station on Friday night. The complainant, an employee of a private company, was travelling in a window seat. A private luxury bus brushed against the PMPML carriage on Pune-Satara Road and the complainant hurled abuses at its driver. The luxury bus halted a little distance ahead. Its driver alighted, entered the PMPML bus and allegedly assaulted the complainant.Pawar said, “The complainant wanted to report the incident and came to the police station. At that moment, the police inspector confronted him, asked him why he wanted to lodge a police complaint and slapped him.”He said, “We later registered a non-cognisable offence against the luxury bus driver for allegedly beating up the PMPML bus passenger.”DCP (Zone II) Mohite said, “The inspector was recently transferred to Pune city police. Earlier, he was posted with the Gadchiroli police.”
Article Summary: An inspector of Sahakarnagar police station assaulted a complainant on the station premises allegedly in an inebriated state on Friday night. He has also been booked under the Maharashtra Prohibition Act. Assistant commissioner of police Gajanan Pawar is conducting an inquiry against the inspector.

Article Title: Four held with MD worth Rs2.5 lakh in Bhusawal raid
Article Text:
Nashik:





The Bhusawal Taluka police arrested four people during a late-night raid near Kinhi MIDC on Friday and seized 62.21 grams of mephedrone (MD) worth Rs 2.48 lakh. The police also seized two motorcycles and four cellphones, taking the total value of the confiscated items to over Rs 7.2 lakh.Acting on specific information, a team comprising personnel from the Bhusawal Taluka police and the Local Crime Branch (LCB), led by probationary sub-divisional police officer and in-charge of Bhusawal Taluka police station Prashant Darekar, raided the location at around 2.55am.The police arrested four suspects identified as Rishabh Kunal Khedkar (18), Prathamesh Dilip Awhad (27), Shaikh Afzal Shaikh Rehmatullah (26) and Asgarkhan Anwarkhan (57), all residents of different parts of Bhusawal.During the raid, the police seized 62.21 grams of MD, classified as a commercial quantity, worth Rs 2.48 lakh. They also confiscated two motorcycles valued at Rs 3.25 lakh and four cellphones worth Rs 1.55 lakh.The Bhusawal Taluka police registered a case under relevant sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.SP Shrikant Dhivare told reporters that strict action against drug peddling, storage and transportation across Jalgaon district would be a continuous process to make the district drug-free.Meanwhile, the Jamner police seized over 13kg of ganja from a farm in the taluka. Acting on specific information, a police team raided the farm and found cannabis plants worth over Rs 3.35 lakh.The farm owner fled the spot. The Jamner police have registered a case against the farmer under relevant sections of the NDPS Act and launched a search for him.
Article Summary: The Bhusawal Taluka police arrested four people during a late-night raid near Kinhi MIDC on Friday and seized 62.21 grams of mephedrone (MD) worth Rs 2.48 lakh. The police also seized two motorcycles and four cellphones, taking the total value of the confiscated items to over Rs 7.2 lakh.

Article Title: Father is natural guardian, but can’t take forced custody of child, says Madras HC
Article Text: Chennai: A father, despite being a natural guardian, cannot take forcible custody of his children. It must be sought in accordance with the procedure established by law, Madras high court has said.A division bench of justices A D Jagadish Chandira and Justice B Karthikeyan made the observation on Thursday while ordering a Puducherry man to hand back his two and a half-year-old child to his wife.The court passed the order on a habeas corpus plea moved by the wife, a doctor practising in Chennai. She submitted that her marriage was solemnised on Jan 21, 2021 and the couple had two children born in 2023 and 2024. Later, citing cruelty and harassment, she had separated from him and was staying with her mother.While her plea seeking divorce is pending consideration before a family court, she alleged that on Aug 28, 2026, her husband forced into her parental home and forcibly took away their two-and-half-year-old child, without her consent. Aggrieved, she lodged a complaint with the all women police but no action was taken, she said.Recording the submissions, the court said: “Though the husband is the father and natural guardian of the child who is just about two-and-a-half years old, the custody of the minor child cannot be taken by force and it must be sought in accordance with the procedure established by law.”
Article Summary: A father, despite being a natural guardian, cannot take forcible custody of his children, Madras high court has said. A division bench of justices A D Jagadish Chandira and Justice B Karthikeyan made the observation on Thursday. The court passed the order on a habeas corpus plea moved by the wife.

Article Title: Crackdown on hookah bars in city; 13 booked after raids
Article Text:
Chennai:





Greater Chennai Police, in coordination with the state health department, registered cases against operators of 13 hookah bars following inspections at 14 establishments across the city.The inspections were conducted by a team under the supervision of deputy commissioners of police. They inspected hookah bars in Teynampet, Vepery, Nungambakkam, Egmore, Anna Salai, Mylapore and Royapettah.The teams checked whether the establishments had valid licences and complied with govt regulations. They also examined whether prohibited tobacco products or narcotic substances were being used on the premises.Based on suspected violations, police registered 13 cases against the operators of 13 establishments and seized equipment used for smoking hookah. The seized materials were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for examination.The police also cautioned the public, especially youngsters, against using prohibited tobacco products and narcotic substances, citing the health risks associated with their consumption.
Article Summary: Greater Chennai Police, in coordination with the state health department, registered cases against operators of 13 hookah bars. The inspections were conducted by a team under the supervision of deputy commissioners of police. The teams checked whether the establishments had valid licences and complied with govt regulations.

Article Title: Woman booked for duping Coimbatore rifle shooting coach of Rs 16 lakh
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Singanallur police in Coimbatore have registered a case based on a complaint filed by a female rifle shooting coach who alleged that a woman had cheated her of Rs 16 lakh by promising to settle a land dispute using her political influence.The complainant, R Anu Prabha, 30, of Nanjappa Nagar in Singanallur is a coach at a Rifle Academy near Kuniyamuthur. According to the complaint, her mother, Rajeswari, owns 20 cents of land at Kannampalayam village in Sulur taluk. However, a civil dispute is pending in connection with the property.In 2024, V G Dhanalakshmi , the mother of one of the students at the rifle academy, approached Anu Prabha and promised to resolve the land dispute by using her political influence. Trusting her assurance, Anu Prabha paid her a total of Rs 16 lakh in several instalments. The amount included Rs 10.95 lakh in cash and Rs 5.05 transferred through UPI.However, Dhanalakshmi failed to resolve the dispute or return the money. When Anu Prabha demanded repayment, the woman reportedly issued cheques, which were subsequently dishonoured due to insufficient funds. The complainant further alleged that the money was used by Dhanalakshmi to produce a film.She lodged a complaint with the Singanallur police on Wednesday, and police registered a case under sections 316(2) and 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and began an investigation.
Article Summary: The complainant, R Anu Prabha, 30, of Nanjappa Nagar in Singanallur is a coach at a Rifle Academy near Kuniyamuthur. According to the complaint, her mother, Rajeswari, owns 20 cents of land at Kannampalayam village in Sulur taluk. A civil dispute is pending in connection with the property.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Nainar questions delay in ordering probe into library scam
Article Text:
Nainar questions delay in ordering probe into library scam





Tirunelveli: BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran on Saturday questioned the state govt's alleged reluctance to order an inquiry into irregularities in Periyar Arivulagam library project, and demanded immediate action if corruption charges were proven.He told reporters in Tirunelveli that successive govts had misused the name of Periyar, and claimed that a major scam had taken place in the procurement of books for the library. “Even after a committee member exposed the alleged corruption, the ruling govt has not initiated any action. Why has no case been registered so far,” he said.On the political front, Nainar accused the TVK govt of engaging in horse-trading and attempting to secure legislative support by attracting elected representatives from rival parties. He ruled out contesting the anticipated Ambasamudram byelection.
Article Summary: BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran questions delay in ordering probe into library scam. He claims that a major scam had taken place in the procurement of books for the library. He accused the TVK govt of engaging in horse-trading and attempting to secure legislative support.

Article Title: Fire destroys cracker shop near Theni, 4 injured
Article Text:
A fire broke out at a licensed firecracker shop and godown at Kamatchipuram village near Chinnamanur in Theni district around midnight on Friday





Theni: A massive fire gutted a firecracker shop near Chinnamanur in Theni district late on Friday, destroying fireworks worth several lakhs of rupees. Four workers escaped with minor injuries.The shop owned by Alagumuthu was located on Poomalaikundu Road. It had a retail outlet in the front and two storage godowns at the rear. Alagumuthu has been engaged in firecracker business for over a decade, procuring fireworks in bulk from Sivakasi Police said the fire began around 12am in the godowns, subsequently spreading to the shop premises and engulfing it soon. Four shop workers sustained minor injuries and were admitted to Theni Medical College Hospital while most others present managed to escape before the fire. A pick-up vehicle and two lorries loaded with firecrackers were parked on the premises. The pick-up vehicle was completely gutted. Fire and rescue services personnel from Chinnamanur, Theni, Bodinayakanur and Palayam battled the flames.Odaipatti police have registered a case and are investigating whether the fire was caused by an electrical short circuit or any other reason.. Uthamapalayam DSP Chandrasekar and revenue divisional officer Syed Mohammed conducted a preliminary inquiry. Theni district superintendent of police K S Praveen Gowtham also visited the spot and reviewed the situation.
Article Summary: Fire broke out at a licensed firecracker shop and godown at Kamatchipuram village near Chinnamanur in Theni district around midnight on Friday. Four workers escaped with minor injuries. Police are investigating whether the fire was caused by an electrical short circuit or any other reason.

Article Title: Mannan appears before CCB, says will face case legally
Article Text:
Mannan appears before CCB, says will face case legally





Madurai: AIADMK functionary and former deputy mayor of Madurai corporation P M Mannan, who was arrested in the alleged cash-for-vote controversy involving TVK MLA V M S Mustafa, on Saturday said he would face the case legally. He was speaking to reporters after appearing before Madurai Central Crime Branch (CCB) police for questioning in this connection.Mannan was arrested based on Mustafa’s complaint that he allegedly offered him Rs 30 crore to vote against the TVK govt in a proposed no-confidence motion. A special court later released him on a personal bond. On Saturday, Mannan was questioned for nearly four-and-a-half hours based on the MLA's complaint and information provided by his (MLA’s ) aide, Kani Raja, during earlier inquiries."I answered all the questions raised by the investigating officers. The inquiry was conducted properly,” Mannan told reporters. "I am ready to appear whenever I am summoned. I will handle the case legally. I have faced several politically motivated cases and will face this one as well through legal means," he said.Asked about Mustafa's claim that he possessed audio evidence related to the alleged offer, Mannan said, "You should ask him that question."
Article Summary: AIADMK functionary and former deputy mayor of Madurai corporation P M Mannan was arrested in the alleged cash-for-vote controversy involving TVK MLA V M S Mustafa. Mannan appeared before Madurai Central Crime Branch (CCB) police for questioning in this connection.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: Meenangadi school trip row: Pocso case filed over social media abuse
Article Text:
Kozhikode

:





A Pocso case has been registered against individuals accused of abusing students on social media following the controversy surrounding a school excursion organised by Meenangadi GHSS School. The action was taken based on a complaint filed by the UDF functionaries in Meenangadi. The case has been registered under provisions of the Information Technology Act and Pocso Act Facebook accounts that allegedly posted abusive remarks are under the surveillance of the cyber police. Those who posted offensive comments or uploaded content targeting the children are likely to face action, police said. The case has been registered under Section 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Section 67B of the Information Technology Act, and Sections 11(i) and 12 of the Pocso Act for allegedly abusing children below the age of 18 through social media.The row pertains to the principal of GHSS, Meenangadi, in Wayanad, facing allegations that he had consumed alcohol during a school excursion to Hyderabad along with the PTA president. A blood test report had later cleared him of the same.
Article Summary: The action was taken based on a complaint filed by the UDF functionaries in Meenangadi. Facebook accounts that allegedly posted abusive remarks are under the surveillance of the cyber police. Those who posted offensive comments or uploaded content targeting the children are likely to face action, police said.

Article Title: Desh Bachao rally by Congress draws thousands in Kozhikode
Article Text:
Kozhikode

:





Thousands of people participated in the Desh Bachao rally organised by Congress in Kozhikode in solidarity with the nationwide protests led by Rahul Gandhi calling for protection of democracy.The rally began near Mavoor Road Smrithipatham and proceeded towards Kozhikode beach around 5 pm on Saturday. Though rain lashed the city during the procession, the party functionaries continued to lead the rally. Although the police diverted traffic, vehicles remained stuck in several parts of the city for hours. Vehicles carrying Congress workers from the party’s 26 blocks had begun arriving in the city by noon.Addressing a public meeting held in connection with the rally, AICC general secretary and MP K C Venugopal said Narendra Modi would become Prime Minister who would be forced to leave office in the most humiliating manner in the country.“More troubles are yet to come for Modi. If there is a May in 2029, Rahul Gandhi will be the Prime Minister. The struggle will continue until Gyanesh Kumar resigns,” Venugopal said.He alleged that Modi had attempted to eliminate Congress through electoral manipulation by placing Kumar at the forefront. “BJP’s slogan of a ‘Congress-mukt Bharat’ was part of this effort,” he said.The MP added that Kumar was among the most corrupt officials Kerala has seen. He was also responsible for dividing Jammu & Kashmir for Modi. “Legal protection was granted to Kumar. Even the President of India, Prime Minister and Chief Justice of India do not enjoy such protection. This was done to facilitate electoral manipulation and undermine democracy,” Venugopal added.
Article Summary: Thousands of people participated in the Desh Bachao rally organised by Congress in Kozhikode. The rally was in solidarity with the nationwide protests led by Rahul Gandhi calling for protection of democracy. Though rain lashed the city during the procession, the party functionaries continued to lead the rally.

Article Title: Messi row: TV channel chief moves Kerala HC to quash FIR
Article Text:
Kochi:





Anto Augustine, managing director of Malayalam news channel Reporter TV, has approached the high court seeking to quash an FIR registered against him over alleged financial misappropriation in connection with an unsuccessful attempt to bring the Argentine national football team and its former captain Lionel Messi to Kochi.A bench of Justice P V Balakrishnan on Friday issued notice to the state govt on the petition and sought its instructions by Nov 23. The FIR was registered at Kalamassery police station and is being investigated by a special investigation team (SIT). The case relates to alleged financial irregularities in connection with plans to organise an international football match in Kochi featuring the Argentine national team and Messi.According to the FIR, Augustine entered into a criminal conspiracy on Dec 20, 2024, by incorporating allegedly false and fabricated details into an agreement signed with the Argentina Football Association, with the intention of cheating the state govt and the public. The FIR further alleged that he conspired to secure custody of the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium at Kaloor by obtaining an exemption from the requirement to furnish a security deposit of Rs 5 crore on Sept 26, 2025.Challenging the FIR, Augustine contended that it amounted to an abuse of the process of law as the allegations did not disclose the essential ingredients of the offences of cheating or criminal conspiracy.
Article Summary: Anto Augustine, managing director of Malayalam news channel Reporter TV, has approached the high court seeking to quash an FIR registered against him over alleged financial misappropriation. The case relates to alleged financial irregularities in connection with plans to organise an international football match in Kochi featuring the Argentine national team and Messi.
